name: Island Pacific Distributors
old_description: Founded on October 2, 1978 by Barbara and Leon Wolfley, Island Pacific Distributors (IPD) began our humble beginnings at our King Street location, opening our doors to customers as a Wholesale Hardware and Locksmith Supply Company. IPD concentrated on supplying high security keys and locks for perimeter doors on many of the high-rise condominiums being built during the high-rise boom in Waikiki and along the Ala Wai Corridor. Along with condominiums, we sold to many of the local retail establishments of the time including McDonalds, Liberty House, Gibson’s, Handyman Hardware, Holiday Mart Hardware, Ben Franklin Stores, & J.C. Penny’s.
about:
Island Pacific Distributors was founded on October 2, 1978 by Barbara and Leon Wolfley in Honolulu, Hawaii. The company began as a wholesale hardware and locksmith supply operation on King Street, serving the high-rise condominium boom in Waikiki and the Ala Wai corridor.

Today IPD operates from a 35,000-square-foot facility on Alakawa Street that houses offices, a warehouse, a showroom, and a steel door and frame fabrication shop staffed by two certified welders. The shop holds the state's only Warnock Hersey Mark certification from Intertek for constructing and modifying Assa Abloy's Curries line of hollow metal doors and frames. The company distributes doors, frames, finish hardware, security products, and specialty building products, and provides consultation, design, specification writing, installation, maintenance, electronic access control, and locksmith services. It has completed hundreds of projects and distributed millions of products across the islands.

IPD serves architects, general contractors, facility owners, and management companies in Hawaii's hospitality, commercial construction, government, luxury residential, and condominium sectors. Notable projects include the Allure Waikiki, Moana Surfrider, Sheraton Moana Surfrider, Four Seasons Resort Lanai, Disney Aulani Resort, Kapolei Judiciary Complex, and Kamehameha Schools.

The company's "Find A Way" motto reflects its commitment to customer service and problem-solving. Its differentiators include being Hawaii's only certified Architectural Hardware Consultant, exclusive distributor for Sargent Hardware, Smoke Guard, CornellCookson, and Total Door Openings System, and an employee-owned structure that aligns staff incentives with long-term client relationships.

name: J & O Plastics
old_description: J&O Plastics specializes in plastic injection molding solutions for plastic shipping products and the logistics industry.
about:
J & O Plastics operates from a 250,000-square-foot facility in Rittman, Ohio, a location chosen for its access to the northern Ohio retail distribution corridor. The company was founded in 1982 by Oscar and Christine Gross, initially supplying injection-molded parts to the Mr. Coffee Company.

The core operation is custom plastic injection molding, with a specialty in clear resins. J & O is one of the few U.S. molders running a proprietary process for straight PET, a BPA-free, low-cost clear plastic, alongside acrylic, polypropylene, SAN, crystal styrene, PVC, ABS, LDPE, and HDPE. The plant handles large-part molding and provides in-line assembly, kitting, packaging, barcoding, warehousing, inventory management, and direct shipment to major retailers.

Customers span household goods, industrial, agricultural, medical, and shipping/logistics sectors. The company is certified to ship directly to Amazon FBA, Costco, Walmart, Target, and Bed Bath & Beyond, handling SKU management, UPC barcoding, and bulk packaging for those accounts. It also serves OEM industrial applications requiring precision-molded components.

The founders’ early focus on PET was driven by demand for durable, BPA-free clear products. That proprietary PET process, combined with automation, allows competitive pricing. A sustainability pledge keeps scrap below 1 percent, with all waste either resold or recycled, and cardboard baled daily for recycling.

name: J & R Senior Sheetmetal, Inc.
old_description: J&R Senior Sheetmetal Inc., a family-owned and operated business in Westerly, Rhode Island, specializes in custom copper work. Serving most of Rhode Island, including Block Island, we bring 30 years of metal experience across three generations and over 40 years of roofing expertise to ensure your home stays dry. We take pride in tackling the unique challenges of building coastal homes and prioritize providing quality service and products that withstand the harsh New England weather. If you can build it, we can cover it (in metal, of course). Over the past 30 years, we have earned a reputation for using innovative approaches to help our clients achieve their goals. We provide exceptional customer service and work closely with builders, roofers, and homeowners to fully understand their needs and expectations.
about:
J & R Senior Sheetmetal, Inc. operates from Westerly, Rhode Island, as a family-owned business now in its third generation. The company traces its roots to over 40 years of roofing expertise and three decades of metalworking experience, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. It began as a specialist in custom copper work for the coastal communities of Rhode Island, including Block Island.

The shop fabricates a range of sheet metal components for roofing and flashing applications. Core products include copper roof vents, wall vents, drip edges, valleys, window and door pans, shower pans, step flashing, chimney caps, scuppers, and radius flashing, all produced in 16-ounce copper and Freedom Gray zinc-copper alloy. The company also works in .032-inch painted aluminum for drip edges, drip caps, valleys, and step flashing. Beyond custom fabrication, J & R Senior Sheetmetal assembles standing seam roof bundles that package high-temperature ice-and-water shield, wall flashings, panels, clips, screws, Z-bar, and ridge caps. It also acts as a distributor for Wuko hand tools and PREFA roofing systems.

The customer base centers on residential builders, roofing contractors, and homeowners throughout Rhode Island, with a focus on the challenges of coastal construction. The company's work is tailored to withstand New England weather, and its portfolio includes standing seam roofs, flat-pounded roofing, cupolas, chimney through-flashings, and radius roofs.

J & R Senior Sheetmetal emphasizes domestic production, noting that its products are made in the USA using a mix of antique hand tools and modern machinery. The firm highlights quick turnaround times and a collaborative approach with builders and roofers to address the unique demands of seaside architecture.

name: J R Plastics and Machining
old_description: Since 1994, JR Plastics & Machining, Inc. has provided custom vacuum forming for North America. Utilizing reliable and accurate equipment, we produce quality parts with very little down time.
about:
JR Plastics & Machining, Inc. operates from Lowesville, Virginia, in the Blue Ridge Mountains about 25 miles south of Charlottesville. The business traces its roots to 1994 when it began as a custom vacuum forming firm. In 1998 the owners, David Trent and Raymond Schneider, incorporated the company and added a full CNC machine shop, enabling them to produce molds and secondary processes in-house. The two owners remain the primary contacts for every project.

The shop provides custom vacuum forming, hotwire bending, and CNC machining under one roof. Vacuum forming capacity reaches 24 by 50 inches with a 9-inch draw depth in plastics up to 0.250 inch thick, including PETG, PVC, ABS, polycarbonate (Kydex), polystyrene, acrylic, and HDPE. CNC machining handles parts up to 50 by 100 by 9 inches in aluminum, brass, and stainless steel. Equipment includes HAAS mills, lathes, and routers, plus custom-built forming and bending machines that the team maintains themselves to minimize downtime.

Customers span medical, electronics, food packaging, and sports performance sectors across North America. The company works directly with clients from prototype through large-scale production runs, offering engineering support to refine designs for cost and performance.

The firm differentiates itself by keeping the entire production process — mold making, forming, machining, and finishing — in a single facility, with an owner serving as the direct point of contact. Over 100 years of combined experience in vacuum forming, pressure forming, hotwire bending, and CNC programming underpins their ability to deliver quick turnaround on tooling and parts.

name: J&L Plastic Molding
old_description: We specialize in transitioning injection molding projects to reach the next level in development and production.
about:
J&L Plastic Molding operates from Wallingford, Connecticut, where it runs a dedicated injection molding facility. The company focuses on transitioning molding projects from development into full-scale production, offering prototype and production tooling, injection molding, and insert molding.

Its core services include prototype and production tooling, injection molding, insert molding, and tool transfer. The shop occupies two buildings housing 28 injection molding machines with clamp forces from 28 to 385 tons and shot capacities of 0.6 to 24 ounces, enabling a range of part sizes and volumes. The facility is geared for both prototype and production runs.

The company primarily serves medical device manufacturers. A notable customer is LeMaitre Vascular, which recognized J&L as its Supplier of the Year for quality, delivery, innovation, and collaboration. J&L's ISO 13485:2016 certification underscores its focus on medical-grade quality.

J&L emphasizes its expertise with engineered thermoplastic resins such as PEEK (Victrex), PEI (Ultem), PPSU (Radel), PPS (Ryton), LCP (Vectra), TPU, TPE, polycarbonate, and ABS. Its quality management system is certified to ISO 13485:2016 by NQA, supporting medical-grade production requirements.

about:
J-Tech Construction & Solar was founded in 2004 in Lincoln, Nebraska. The company began as a roofing contractor and has operated continuously in the Lincoln and Grand Island areas for over two decades.

The firm provides a full range of exterior services for residential and commercial properties, including roofing (asphalt, metal, storm damage restoration), siding (seamless steel, metal, James Hardie fiber cement, vinyl), windows, doors, gutter systems, and solar panel installation. A distinguishing feature is its in-house metal fabrication capability, producing custom metal roofing and siding components for each project rather than relying on pre-manufactured panels. The company also employs drone technology for roof assessments.

J-Tech serves homeowners and commercial building owners across Nebraska (excluding the panhandle) and parts of Iowa, Kansas, South Dakota, and Missouri. Its customer base includes property owners in Lincoln, Omaha, Grand Island, Kearney, Hastings, and surrounding communities seeking roofing, siding, window, door, gutter, and solar solutions. The company works with insurance restoration projects as well.

The company emphasizes several differentiators: single-contractor accountability for all exterior trades without subcontractors, drone inspections that document conditions before work begins, certified installer status with ProVia and James Hardie, a Nebraska contractor registration, warranty-backed installations, free inspections and estimates, and financing options for large projects.

name: JCS Technologies Inc.
old_description: JCS Technologies specializes in high-quality wire harness design, prototyping and manufacturing.
about:
Founded in 2011 in Las Vegas, Nevada, JCS Technologies operates as a contract manufacturer specializing in wire harness design, prototyping, and production. The company has grown from its inception to serve clients requiring fast turnaround and low-volume runs with stringent quality requirements.

JCS Technologies provides end-to-end wire harness services, including design assistance, rapid prototyping with no minimum order quantities, and full-scale manufacturing. Every harness undergoes 100% individual testing before shipment, backed by a 0% failure rate guarantee that includes free replacement within 48 hours. The company recently expanded into a larger facility to support its focus on quick-turn, high-reliability projects.

The company serves the gaming, renewable energy, industrial, and amusement sectors. In gaming, it produces harnesses for casino equipment; in renewable energy, for controllers and generators; in industrial, for consumer electronics, kiosks, ATMs, and computers; and in amusement, for audio, video, control, and payment systems. Notable customers include Light & Wonder and Asahi Seiko.

JCS Technologies was built on a philosophy of eliminating unacceptable failure rates. Its quality program reflects accountability to both the customer and itself, with cross-trained professionals overseeing each production stage. The firm emphasizes that cost savings are meaningless if components prove unreliable, and it maintains UL and RoHS compliance to meet industry regulations.

The company designs, fabricates, installs, maintains, repairs, and retrofits custom tension fabric storage buildings for bulk material storage. It also produces consumer products such as steel benches and fire pits, provides general contracting services for municipalities, and executes large-scale commercial customizations. From its Bella Vista facility, JPM employs multiple full-time steel fabricators, installation specialists, and office staff, serving customers across the continental United States. All buildings are engineer-approved and carry a 25-year warranty, with the first two years of maintenance included.

JPM serves agriculture (grain, hay, equipment storage), government and municipalities (salt, sand, maintenance buildings), waste and recycling, aviation (aircraft hangars), mining, equestrian facilities, port and intermodal transport, and railroad transportation.

McGary started the business to fill a local skills gap and to pass down trade traditions. The company emphasizes integrity, hands-on oversight by the founder on every project, and a "cut materials, not corners" philosophy. Its differentiators include the 25-year warranty, included maintenance, engineer-approved designs, and veteran-owned, family-operated values.

about:
Kaempf & Harris Sheet Metal operates from Frederick, Maryland, where it was founded in 1941 as part of the R.W. Warner family of companies. The business reached its third generation of family ownership in 1998 when Matt Warner became CEO, continuing a lineage that traces back to 1937 under the Warner name. Today it functions as a division alongside Warner Service, Warner Construction, and Warner Mechanical.

The shop focuses on precision sheet metal fabrication for commercial, industrial, and institutional projects. Core processes include CNC laser cutting, press brake forming, turret punching, welding, riveting, and fastening, with finishing options such as painting, powder coating, and galvanizing. The company reports fabricating more than 500 tons of metal annually—aluminum, steel, copper, stainless steel, galvanized steel, and black iron—and cites a single project, Frederick’s Rose Hill Cancer Center, that required over 75,000 pounds of sheet metal. Design-build services integrate design and construction under a single point of contact, and crews also handle on-site installation of the fabricated components.

Customers span mechanical contractors, general contractors, corporations, and institutions across healthcare, sports and entertainment, commercial construction, industrial manufacturing, and infrastructure. Notable references include the Rose Hill Cancer Center and the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports Event Center, a $59.5 million project authorized by the Maryland Stadium Authority in 2021.

Kaempf & Harris emphasizes a design-build model that streamlines delivery and reduces rework, backed by American Institute of Steel Construction (AISC) fabricator certification and active membership in the Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors’ National Association (SMACNA). A dedicated in-house safety program, including OSHA 10/30 and specialized trade training, supports its focus on mission-critical environments where uptime and coordination are essential.

name: Kamuela Hardwoods
old_description: Kamuela Hardwoods in Kamuela, HI specializes in reclaimed Hawaiian timber, live-edge slabs, and premium hardwood lumber for furniture makers, woodworkers, instrument builders, and artisans. Our sawmill salvages urban and felled trees, turning them into high-quality wood while supporting sustainable forestry practices. We offer over 30 Hawaiian and exotic
about:
Kamuela Hardwoods operates from Waimea, Hawaii, where co-owners Alex Woodbury and Joshua Greenspan—an ISA‑certified arborist—founded the company as a partnership between an arborist and a woodworker. The business began with a mission to salvage urban and felled trees that would otherwise be burned, chipped, or landfilled, turning that material into usable lumber.

The sawmill processes over 30 Hawaiian and exotic hardwood species—including koa, monkeypod, mango, Norfolk pine, lychee, eucalyptus, and ohia—into live‑edge slabs, kiln‑dried lumber, and bowl blanks. A kiln‑drying step ensures dimensional stability for fine woodworking and instrument making. The operation runs on locally produced bio‑diesel and follows a zero‑waste model: offcuts become utility lumber or garden materials, while sawdust and chips are converted to mulch and soil amendments.

Customers include furniture makers, woodworkers, instrument builders, artisans, and builders across Hawaii, the continental U.S., and internationally. The company ships slabs and lumber for cabinetry, countertops, flooring, and custom projects, with an online inventory that allows buyers to select specific pieces.

Woodbury and Greenspan frame the venture as a deliberate alternative to unnecessary tree removal: "We are trying to do something different, we don't want to unnecessarily remove a tree for any reason," Woodbury says. Greenspan adds, "It's unfortunate when a tree has to come down, but in a sense, we're giving it a new life." That ethos drives the salvage‑first approach and the minimal‑waste processing.

Founded in 1962, Kennedy, Gustafson & Cole (KGC) has operated from a 35,000-square-foot facility in Berlin, Connecticut. KGC designs, fabricates, and installs dust collection systems that meet NFPA standards for combustible dust and OSHA regulations for crystalline silica. The company also provides commercial HVAC equipment such as rooftop air handlers, exhaust fans, smoke/fire dampers, and VAV boxes, along with custom sheet metal fabrication in galvanized steel, carbon steel, aluminum, stainless steel, PVC, and polypropylene. Its 35,000-square-foot plant houses in-house fabrication capabilities, allowing the firm to handle projects from ductwork and pipe fittings to complete baghouse collectors.

The company serves aerospace manufacturers, having designed a wet collection system for magnesium dust at an aerospace facility, and works with industrial clients on heat recovery and energy savings projects. Its customer base also includes commercial building owners and property managers seeking HVAC solutions, as well as industrial process facilities requiring custom ventilation and dust control.

KGC emphasizes staying current with technological developments in air pollution control, offering engineering expertise to determine compliance requirements and prepare cost-effective recommendations. The firm highlights its in-house fabrication and broad supplier network as enabling rapid response, and notes that every installation is fully guaranteed.

Kindel Grand Rapids, based in Grand Rapids, Michigan, traces its roots to 1886 when Albert F. Karges began making furniture in Evansville, Indiana. The modern entity formed when Kindel Furniture (founded 1901 by Charles J. Kindel) acquired Karges and Councill Furniture (founded 1973 by Fred and Hope Councill). The Fisher family has owned the business since 1964, maintaining a family-owned, 100% American-made operation.

The company produces made-to-order, handcrafted luxury furniture from its Grand Rapids facility. Offerings span dining, occasional, bedroom, and workspace collections, each built to customer specifications. The operation emphasizes domestic production, using traditional woodworking methods rather than offshore manufacturing.

Customers include residential clients seeking signature pieces and commercial offices requiring custom desks, tables, and credenzas. The Councill line has served workplace needs since 1973, while the Kindel and Karges brands address high-end home furnishings.

Kindel Grand Rapids differentiates itself through a commitment to domestic craftsmanship, preserving over 300 years of collective experience across its three heritage brands. The company states that every piece is made to precise customer specifications in its Michigan workshop, rejecting lower-cost offshore alternatives.

about:
Kulite Semiconductor Products, Inc. was founded in 1959 by Dr. Anthony D. Kurtz in Leonia, New Jersey, just outside New York City. A physicist with degrees from MIT, Dr. Kurtz left Honeywell to establish a high‑technology company focused on pressure transduction. The business remains family‑founded and woman‑owned, now led by his widow, Nora Kurtz.

The company designs and manufactures pressure transducers, sensors, and switches for extreme environments. Its product line spans pressure ranges from 1 to 60,000 PSI, operating temperatures from ‑320 °F to 932 °F, and configurations including submersible, redundant, and hermetically sealed units. Kulite holds over 400 patents and operates a 200,000‑square‑foot, three‑building campus that houses research, manufacturing, and corporate offices, employing over 800 people.

Kulite serves aerospace and defense (commercial airliners such as the Boeing 747, military aircraft), automotive test and motorsport (Formula One, IndyCar), space exploration, marine, oil exploration, coal mining, and process‑control industries. Customers include OEMs, racing teams, and government agencies requiring high‑reliability pressure measurement.

The firm emphasizes that its differentiation lies in solving difficult pressure‑measurement problems: "whenever pressure or force needs to be measured, Kulite comes up with a solution." It claims to be the world’s largest supplier of aerospace transducers and points to its ongoing R&D investment, university partnerships, and thousands of custom designs delivered since 1959.

old_description: In 1885, civil engineer Leprilete Sweet founded L. Sweet & Company, in the Olneyville section of Providence, RI.
about:
L. Sweet Lumber Company Inc. traces its roots to 1885 when civil engineer Leprilete Sweet founded L. Sweet & Company in the Olneyville section of Providence, Rhode Island. Sweet purchased a wooden frame building from the Church of the Messiah, moved it to Harris Avenue for railroad access, and established a storefront that remains in use today. The business, now in its fifth generation, continues as a local, family-owned operation.

The company stocks framing and finish lumber sourced from domestic and international forests, and maintains an extensive inventory of moulding profiles, including historical patterns specific to the Providence area. It also supplies doors, windows, skylights, hardwood flooring, decking (as a TimberTech/Azek dealer), cedar shingles, clapboard siding, and a range of building materials. Services include on-time delivery via a fleet of trucks, trade credit, estimates, site visits, contractor referrals, blade sharpening, key cutting, lock keying, and a showroom with displays and samples.

L. Sweet Lumber serves the building and construction industry across Southern New England, catering to contractors, builders, and homeowners.

The company emphasizes its long-standing commitment to service, selection, quality, and competitive pricing, noting that customer loyalty has persisted since its founding. It positions itself as a one-stop shop for lumber and building materials, backed by knowledgeable staff and personalized service.

Lacerta Group, LLC. is headquartered in Mansfield, Massachusetts, and traces its roots to 1993 when the Lotfi family founded the company in Boston’s empowerment zone. The business began as a thermoforming operation that quickly incorporated recycled plastic material. In 2020, the Lotfi family sold a majority stake to SK Capital Partners but remained involved in strategy and operations.

The company manufactures thermoformed PET packaging for food applications, offering both stock and custom solutions. Its fully integrated platform covers in-house design, tooling, printing, and film-sealable and tamper-evident formats. Lacerta operates seven U.S. facilities — three in Mansfield, plus sites in Chatsworth, California; Attleboro, Massachusetts; and Portage, Wisconsin — and maintains an on-site warehouse for immediate shipment of hundreds of stock items. The company reports having recycled more than 150 million pounds of plastic since inception and holds SQF certification for food packaging manufacturing.

Lacerta serves commercial food producers, supermarkets, and convenience-store chains, supplying containers for grab-and-go items such as sandwiches, salads, snacks, and prepared meals. Its packaging is designed to extend shelf life and provide crystal-clear product visibility.

The company differentiates itself through its ReCERTA™ material, which guarantees an average of at least 10% post-consumer recycled content across all PET products, with custom blends available. Lacerta also emphasizes speed to market, sustainability consulting (including life-cycle assessments), and a partnership model that spans the entire product lifecycle.

about:
LadyBug Technologies, LLC is headquartered in Boise, Idaho, after relocating from Santa Rosa, California in 2021. The company was founded in 2004 by two microwave engineers, Richard Hawkins and Jon Sigler, who shared a passion for quality microwave test instrumentation. Hawkins serves as president, bringing four decades of RF and microwave test and measurement experience from Sonoma County, while Sigler, a retired vice president and U.S. Marine veteran with calibration lab experience, contributed software and firmware expertise.

The company designs, develops, and manufactures a broad line of USB power sensors that function as complete, self-contained power measurement solutions without a separate power meter. Its portfolio spans True RMS, peak/pulse/average, pulse profiling, and small form factor sensors covering 4 kHz to 67 GHz with 86 dB dynamic range. The LB5900 series adds optional I2C and SPI connectivity and Linux compatibility. LadyBug also operates a calibration service providing NIST-traceable certificates, a power sensor rental program, and accessories. The 2021 move to Boise doubled the facility footprint, increased manufacturing capacity by 30%, and expanded the product engineering team.

LadyBug’s sensors serve general-purpose RF power testing, automated test equipment (ATE), defense, and portable or compact applications across the microwave and RF test industry.

The company was created to deliver a better product at a better price, built in the U.S.A. Its patented NoZero NoCal technology eliminates user zeroing before measurement, reduces the need for switches and cables in low-level ATE setups, and provides thermal stabilization to prevent drift. The integrated sensor architecture removes the uncertainty of a separate meter and consolidates calibration into a single device.

name: Lakeside Trading, Sheds & Outdoor Furniture
about:
Lakeside Trading LLC has operated from Narragansett, Rhode Island since 1999, when founder Dave Harrigan liquidated his 401(k) to purchase a trailer load of hand-made clay chimineas from Mexico. The family-owned business began as a wholesale and seasonal market venture before Harrigan encountered Pennsylvania shed builders during East Coast buying trips. Recognizing a gap in the Rhode Island market, he acquired a shed-moving trailer and leased a former 19th-century fishing equipment warehouse on South Pier Road, establishing a permanent location that he purchased outright in 2010.

Today the company maintains a 5,000-square-foot showroom and an expansive display yard staffed by 20 full-time employees, several with more than 15 years of tenure. Lakeside Trading does not manufacture its own products; instead it procures, installs, and services American-made sheds, greenhouses, chicken coops, gazebos, garages, pergolas, playsets, and pavilions, along with outdoor furniture crafted from recycled plastic poly lumber and marine-grade hardware. The team installs more than 1,000 structures and sells over 2,000 furniture pieces each year, and also provides site preparation such as gravel or stone pads, rock pads, and shed relocation services.

The primary customer base is residential homeowners throughout Rhode Island seeking durable outdoor storage and living solutions. Projects range from simple garden sheds and Adirondack chairs to custom-designed pavilions, greenhouses converted into art studios, and chicken coops with epoxy floors and automatic doors. The company also handles used-shed purchases, moving and reinstalling them on prepared foundations.

Lakeside Trading differentiates itself through Amish-crafted structures backed by a 10-year warranty and a lifetime service guarantee, free on-site consultations before purchase, and a commitment to fair pricing. The business remains locally owned and operated, emphasizing personal service from sales through installation.

about:
Lance Industries has been building vacuum meat tumblers in Hartford, Wisconsin since 1985. The company was founded to give U.S. meat processors a durable, reliable alternative to imported equipment, becoming the first American-made meat tumbler on the market. Its designs originated from collaboration with Family Farms Meats and the engineering staff at LMI Manufacturing.

The product line comprises four models ranging from 50 to 1,000 pounds of capacity: the LT-5, LT-15, LT-30, and LT-60. Each unit features variable-speed rotation, a digital timer, built-in vacuum, and wheels that allow it to pass through a standard 32-inch door. Drums are constructed from thicker-gauge steel with removable lids and metal-detectable gaskets for sanitation. More than 3,000 tumblers have been installed worldwide, and the company maintains a fully stocked service and repair department.

Customers include meat markets, grocery stores, butcher shops, delis, restaurants, meat processing facilities, and meat-alternative processors. Testimonials cite operations such as Haun's Meat & Sausage, Bardini's Country Smokehouse, Bob's Processing, Hudson Meats, and Quality Cut Meats. Lance also works with domestic and international dealers and participates in the American Association of Meat Processors and the Wisconsin Association of Meat Processors.

The company emphasizes mobility, durability, and U.S.-based technical support as key differentiators. Its tumblers are engineered to reduce marination and curing times, improve yield, and deliver consistent product quality batch after batch.

Larson's founding premise was to solve a real-world problem: existing trailers could not perform the combined functions required for efficient cable installation. The company emphasizes patented designs that improve crew productivity, durability in harsh conditions, and reliability that helps crews lay more cable in less time. Its stated mission is to drive efficiency and innovation in cable installation by working directly with installation crews to refine equipment.

Secondary services include sonic welding, hot stamping, pad printing, assembly, and packaging.

LeVic serves manufacturers in medical, aerospace, electronics, oil and gas, industrial automation, machinery, and packaging sectors. The firm works with commodity thermoplastics, engineering-grade resins, reinforced materials, and custom color-matched formulations, and offers insert molding as a standard capability.

LeVic emphasizes a "One-Vendor Advantage," managing the entire process from design-for-manufacturability review through tooling, molding, and finishing to eliminate multi-supplier coordination. The company holds ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100D certifications, imposes no minimum order quantities, and returns standard quotes within two to three business days.

about:
Liberate Medical is based in Crestwood, Kentucky. The company develops the VentFree Respiratory Muscle Stimulator, a medical device designed to address respiratory muscle atrophy in mechanically ventilated patients.

The VentFree system uses proprietary non-invasive neuromuscular electrical stimulation to contract the abdominal wall muscles in synchrony with exhalation during mechanical ventilation. Therapy can begin from day one of ventilation while patients are sedated or delirious, and the device is described as quick and simple to use. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are disclosed.

The company serves the critical care and respiratory care segments of the healthcare industry. Its customers include hospitals and ICU teams managing mechanically ventilated patients, particularly those requiring more than four days of ventilation who face high rates of weaning failure and post-discharge complications.

Liberate Medical states that its approach may reduce abdominal muscle atrophy and shorten the duration of mechanical ventilation. A pilot randomized controlled trial found that ventilation duration and ICU length of stay were shorter in patients receiving VentFree stimulation compared to placebo, potentially reducing morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs.

about:
Little Homestead Furniture was founded in 1987 by a local architect in Rockville, Maryland. The independent retailer operates a showroom in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area, specializing in solid American hardwood furniture sourced from domestic manufacturers.

The store carries bedroom, dining, living room, home office, TV/media, and youth bedroom collections. Its inventory is produced by a network of small family-owned factories in New England—particularly Vermont—and additional manufacturing partners in Pennsylvania, Ohio, Indiana, Texas, North Carolina, and Virginia. All pieces are built from solid hardwoods such as cherry, maple, oak, and walnut, and the company offers a made-to-order program that allows dimensional changes, stain adjustments, and feature modifications often at little or no extra cost.

Little Homestead primarily serves residential customers in the D.C. region who favor classic, timeless designs—Shaker, Mission, Arts & Crafts, and contemporary motifs—and who prioritize well-made, domestically produced furniture over mass-market alternatives.

The business positions itself as an antidote to the ubiquitous “distressed” and “weathered” finishes common at large retailers, emphasizing responsibly harvested lumber, traditional joinery (dovetailed drawers, mortise-and-tenon construction), and durable, environmentally friendly finishes. The made-to-order flexibility is cited as a key differentiator.

about:
Malloy Electric traces its roots to 1945, when Emmett and Mary Malloy opened a modest motor repair and electric construction shop in downtown Sioux Falls, South Dakota. The business expanded in 1971 under Garry and Dianne Jacobson, who added retail sales of motors, electrical equipment, and power transmission components. Today the company operates eight Centers of Excellence across a six-state footprint—South Dakota, North Dakota, Nebraska, Iowa, Wyoming, and Montana—with its 150,000-square-foot National Operations Center in Sioux Falls serving as headquarters.

The company provides full-lifecycle services for industrial rotating and control equipment. Its motor repair centers handle units from fractional horsepower through 15,000 HP, following EASA AR100 standards, and its machine shops support gearbox rebuilds covering helical, bevel, worm, planetary, and cycloidal reducers. Malloy also designs and builds UL508A-certified custom control panels, motor control centers, and VFD panels, and offers medium-voltage drive system installation up to 15 kV. The Sioux Falls facility houses a 70,000-pound lifting capacity, an 8-foot VPI tank, and static motor analyzers capable of testing to 30 kV. The company stocks more than 5,000 motors ranging from 1/125 HP to over 2,000 HP.

Malloy serves industrial plants, utilities, electric cooperatives, mines, and processors throughout the northern plains and mountain west. Customers rely on its 24/7 field service dispatched from local centers for motor rewinds, gearbox repairs, VFD commissioning, and predictive maintenance programs that include vibration analysis, thermography, and partial discharge testing.

The firm emphasizes problem-solving over parts replacement, continuous investment in capability (such as laser cladding and facility modernization), proximity to customers for rapid response, documented quality records with warranties, and a commitment to long-term relationships—principles that have sustained eight decades of continuous operation.

Manufacturing Industries, Inc. was founded and incorporated in 1976 by Ronald Quillen in Alderson, West Virginia. Quillen had worked in electronics design, test, and manufacturing since the late 1950s before returning to his hometown to start the company.

The company provides full-service electronic contract manufacturing including automated surface-mount assembly (SMT), thru-hole printed circuit board assembly, prototype and turn-key production assembly, electrical and functional testing, wire harness and cable assemblies, conformal coating, and scheduled delivery. A dedicated prototype and medium-quantity SMT line achieves up to 13,000 placements per hour, with pick-and-place data generated on the fly from a circuit board and bill of materials. That data can then be transferred to high-speed production equipment for larger volumes.

Manufacturing Industries serves medical, military, commercial, industrial, automotive, OEM, and consumer-product customers. Its flexible, high-mix capability targets small- to medium-quantity runs, pre-production test builds, and evaluations, with a path to scale into production quantities.

Mark One Metal Works is a custom metal fabrication and design shop based in Sparks, Nevada. The company was founded in 1996 by Mark, who began his career as a transmission mechanic under his father John. The shop provides machining, welding, tube bending, CNC plasma cutting, and CAD design services, working primarily in aluminum. Equipment includes a Lincoln Electric plasma cutting table. No facility size or headcount is disclosed.

Mark One serves commercial, residential, and industrial clients in the Reno–Sparks area and beyond. Examples include custom railings and stairs for homes, aluminum fabrication for industrial projects, roll cages and lightweight parts for off-road vehicles, and trophies for competitions.

The company emphasizes exceptional design, unmatched quality, great customer service, and unique metalworking concepts, drawing on over 30 years of experience in fabrication, machining, and racing.

Marshall Dry Goods serves quilters, crafters, and retail fabric shops across the United States through its online store and a brick-and-mortar location in Batesville. A wholesale division supplies bulk fabric to retailers and other businesses, while the adjacent Marshall’s Quilt House provides a retreat space for quilting groups.

The company differentiates itself through a focus on comfort and convenience: it offers the widest selection of vitrectomy recovery equipment, includes free accessories such as the MajicView Mirror and Travel Cushion with every rental package, and provides personalized fitting and compassionate customer support throughout the recovery process.

Headquartered in Hudson, New Hampshire, Mercury Systems (operating under the Mecury Commercial Electronics name) designs and manufactures advanced electronics for aerospace and defense missions. The company operates a 50,000-square-foot production facility on its Phoenix campus, which opened recently to expand capacity and accelerate delivery timelines.

Its product portfolio includes direct RF multi-chip modules such as the RFS1140 built on AMD Versal adaptive SoCs, rad-tolerant 6U SpaceVPX processing boards like the SCFE6933, small-form-factor RF subsystems such as the DRF4580L with Intel Agilex 9 FPGAs, and broadband MMIC components for rugged defense environments. The company emphasizes chip-scale integration, open architectures, and model-based systems engineering to move from concept to production quickly.

Mercury serves the aerospace, defense, and space sectors, including missile defense, electronic warfare, and satellite programs. It has supported more than 75 spacecraft across all orbits and claims participation in every Mars mission over the past two decades. Customers include prime contractors and government agencies requiring ITAR-compliant, MIL-STD-qualified hardware for land, sea, air, and space domains.

The firm's Advanced Concepts Group engages early in technology development to shape commercial innovations into operational advantages, a strategy the company says ensures its solutions remain ahead of evolving threat environments.

old_description: Throughout all these years, since 1968, Bo has worked continually; while also developing and testing products to stabilize fractures until they may be examined in the hospital.
about:
Med Tech Sweden, Inc. is based in Geneseo, Illinois, where it has operated since 2008. The company traces its origins to 1968 when founder Bo Rickard E. Renberg, a Swedish Air Force firefighter-EMT and later a registered nurse and mobile intensive care nurse, began developing fracture-stabilization devices. Renberg’s career spanned four decades in emergency medical services across Sweden, including leadership roles in the Swedish Rescue and Emergency Medicine Association and the Nordic Ambulance Cooperation Group.

The firm manufactures patented emergency first-responder equipment designed by Renberg in Sweden and produced in its Geneseo shop from U.S.-sourced materials. Each unit undergoes individual rigorous testing before release. Product lines focus on lightweight, environmentally friendly solutions for fracture stabilization and rescue situations where no satisfactory options previously existed.

Customers include U.S. Olympic teams, professional sports organizations such as the Denver Broncos, Dallas Cowboys, and Dallas Mavericks, major healthcare institutions like UCLA, Vanderbilt, Purdue, Sweden’s Queen Silvia Hospital for Children, and Baltimore’s Children’s Hospital, as well as fire departments (Tampa, FDNY EMS), military branches (U.S. Air Force, Homeland Security), ski patrols (Aspen, Vail, Steamboat Springs), motorsports (FIA European Racing), and humanitarian groups (Red Cross of Iceland and Italy, Swedish Coast Guard).

The company emphasizes that its equipment is the most lightweight, environmentally friendly, and medically safe in its class, a claim rooted in Renberg’s frontline experience and continuous product refinement since 1968.

MedCOR Professionals operates a medical supply store in Scarborough, Maine, where it has served patients and clinics since its founding in 1995. The company does not manufacture products but works directly with vendors to source and distribute a range of home medical supplies, bracing and support products, and pain management solutions. Its services include filing Medicare and insurance claims, managing vendor communications, handling billing, tracking, and returns, and scheduling routine product deliveries for clinics. The Scarborough location functions as a retail and distribution point, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

MedCOR Professionals serves home-care patients, medical clinics, and healthcare providers throughout Maine. Concrete examples from its offerings include post-operative bras for breast surgery recovery, walking boots, and multi-post therapy collars. The company also supplies clinics with scheduled deliveries of equipment and consumables, positioning itself as a single-source partner for both individual patients and institutional customers.

The firm emphasizes personalized, compassionate service as its differentiator, highlighting its ACHC accreditation as evidence of compliance with national quality standards. Its stated mission is to enhance patient care through quality clinic supplies and to provide an exceptional patient experience by handling administrative burdens such as insurance claims and vendor coordination.

name: Medical Device Academy, Inc.
old_description: Are you a start-up device company that needs medical device consulting services and training for an FDA 510k submission?
about:
Medical Device Academy, Inc. operates from Shrewsbury, Vermont, with a fully remote team of ten consultants spread across the Eastern Time Zone, including North Carolina, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Vermont. The founding year is not publicly disclosed, nor is the ownership structure. The firm's principal, Rob Packard, brings over 30 years of medical device, pharmaceutical, and biotechnology experience, including a stint as CEO and co-founder of a laparoscopic imaging start-up in 2004.

The company functions as a quality and regulatory consulting firm specializing in FDA 510(k) submissions using the eSTAR template, FDA pre-submissions via PreSTAR, quality system implementation for FDA, ISO 13485, and MDSAP compliance, and internal quality system audits. It also provides FDA U.S. Agent services, CE Marking technical file preparation, Canadian medical device license applications, and a curated suite of training products—including a 510(k) course series, procedure templates, and on-demand webinars. All work is performed virtually; the firm does not manufacture physical products.

Clients are primarily small and mid-size medical device companies, start-ups with proof-of-concept prototypes, and non-U.S. firms seeking FDA market entry. The academy also serves companies needing continuing education, quality system auditing, and regulatory pathway analysis for U.S., European, and Canadian markets.

The firm differentiates itself with flat-fee pricing—enabled by a narrow focus on 510(k) and De Novo pathways—and a team that has designed and built medical devices, not just advised on them. Packard's background as a former Notified Body lead auditor (2009–2012) and start-up CEO informs a practical, teaching-oriented approach aimed at helping clients avoid costly testing repeats and remediation.
